newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees urgent aid for C.Lyonnais, opens probe.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees urgent aid for C.Lyonnais, opens probe.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had approved 3.9 billion French francs ($765.6 million) in emergency aid for Credit Lyonnais and was opening a probe into new aid measures planned for the embattled bank.
European Union Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said the EU executive had approved the emergency rescue money in order to keep the bank in its current position until the end of the year.
"This money is to maintain the status quo until the end of the year....It's a kind of measure to freeze the situation. Not to let it deteriorate," he told a news conference.
Credit Lyonnais, once the largest bank outside of Japan, is being restructured under the 1995 plan allowing for a maximum of 45 billion French francs in subsidies.
It has become clear, however, that a new plan will have to be drafted if the bank is to avoid slipping again into the red.
Van Miert said the 3.9 billion francs would be taken into consideration during the Commission's probe into any further bailout plan for the bank.

Although he refused to give details of what might or might not be acceptable to the Commission in any bailout plan, Van Miert said putting Credit Lyonnais back on track could require a large amount of money and take hefty divestments in exchange.
"If it is obvious that there is no way around, then looking into further divestment (may be needed)...They should be real and substantive," he said.
